questions.text: दिए गए आरेख में वक्र रेखाएँ समविभव पृष्ठों को निरूपित कर रही हैं । किसी आवेश Q को विभिन्न पथों A, B, C और D पर गति करायी गई है । किस पथ के अनुदिश आवेश पर अधिकतम कार्य किया गया है ?
questions.text_english: In the figure curved lines represent equipotential surfaces. A charge Q is moved along different paths A, B, C and D. The work done on the charge will be maximum along the path

options_english.A: A
options_english.B: B
options_english.C: C
options_english.D: D

questions.solution: Work done on charge Q while moving it between two points equals W = Q(V_final - V_initial). Maximum work is done when the potential difference traversed is maximum. From the figure, path C starts near the 15 V equipotential and ends near the 25 V equipotential, giving a potential difference of 10 V, which is the largest among all paths. Paths A and B span smaller potential differences. Therefore, maximum work is done along path C. Options A, B, and D are incorrect because they cross fewer equipotential surfaces and hence involve smaller potential differences.
questions.solution_hindi: किसी आवेश Q को दो बिन्दुओं के बीच ले जाने पर किया गया कार्य W = Q(V_अंतिम - V_प्रारंभिक) होता है । अधिकतम कार्य तब होगा जब विभवान्तर अधिकतम हो । आरेख से पथ C, 15 V से 25 V तक जाता है जो 10 V का अधिकतम विभवान्तर है। अतः पथ C के अनुदिश अधिकतम कार्य किया जाता है।

questions.text: लम्बाई L और त्रिज्या r के किसी तार का प्रतिरोध R है । समान पदार्थ के निम्नलिखित में से किस तार का प्रतिरोध R/2 होगा ?
questions.text_english: The resistance of a wire of length L and radius r is R. Which one of the following would provide a wire of the same material of resistance R/2 ?

options.A: समान त्रिज्या का लम्बाई में दो गुना तार
options.B: समान त्रिज्या का लम्बाई में आधा तार
options.C: समान लम्बाई का दो गुनी त्रिज्या का तार
options.D: समान लम्बाई का आधी त्रिज्या का तार

options_english.A: Using a wire of same radius and twice the length
options_english.B: Using a wire of same radius and half the length
options_english.C: Using a wire of same length and twice the radius
options_english.D: Using a wire of same length and half the radius

questions.solution: Resistance is given by R = ρL/A = ρL/(πr²). To get R/2, we need to halve the resistance. Option B uses the same radius and half the length: R' = ρ(L/2)/(πr²) = R/2. This is correct. Option A doubles the length, giving 2R. Option C doubles the radius, making A four times larger and giving R/4. Option D halves the radius, making A four times smaller and giving 4R. Hence option B is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: प्रतिरोध R = ρL/(πr²) होता है। R/2 प्राप्त करने के लिए लम्बाई आधी करनी होगी (त्रिज्या समान रखते हुए): R' = ρ(L/2)/(πr²) = R/2। अतः विकल्प B सही है।

questions.text: किसी तार का 1 cm लम्बा कोई खण्ड x-अक्ष के अनुदिश रखा है तथा +x दिशा के अनुदिश इस तार से धारा 0.5 A प्रवाहित हो रही है । इस प्रदेश में किसी चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र B⃗ = (0.4 mT) ĵ + (0.6 mT) k̂ को अनुप्रयुक्त किया गया है । इस तार के खण्ड पर कार्यरत बल है –
questions.text_english: A 1 cm segment of a wire lying along x-axis carries current of 0.5 A along +x direction. A magnetic field B⃗ = (0.4 mT) ĵ + (0.6 mT) k̂ is switched on, in the region. The force acting on the segment is

questions.text: व्यास 15 mm तथा 300 फेरों की किसी कुण्डली को 30 mT के चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र में इस प्रकार रखा गया है कि कुण्डली का तल चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र की दिशा के लम्बवत हो । क्षेत्र की तीव्रता को एकसमान रूप से घटाते हुए 20 ms में शून्य कर दिया गया और फिर से एकसमान रूप से 40 ms में 30 mT तक बढ़ाया गया । यदि दो समय अन्तरालों में प्रेरित emf क्रमश: e₁ और e₂ हैं तो e₁/e₂ का मान है –
questions.text_english: A circular coil of diameter 15 mm having 300 turns is placed in a magnetic field of 30 mT such that the plane of the coil is perpendicular to the direction of magnetic field. The magnetic field is reduced uniformly to zero in 20 ms and again increased uniformly to 30 mT in 40 ms. If the emfs induced in the two time intervals are e₁ and e₂ respectively, then the value of e₁/e₂ is
questions.solution: The induced emf is e = N × A × (ΔB/Δt). The area A and number of turns N are the same in both cases. For the first interval: ΔB/Δt = 30 mT / 20 ms = 1.5 T/s, so e₁ = NA × 1.5. For the second interval: ΔB/Δt = 30 mT / 40 ms = 0.75 T/s, so e₂ = NA × 0.75. Therefore e₁/e₂ = 1.5/0.75 = 2. Options A, B, and D are incorrect as they correspond to wrong ratios of the rates of change of flux.
questions.solution_hindi: e = N×A×(ΔB/Δt)। e₁ के लिए ΔB/Δt = 30/20 = 1.5 T/s; e₂ के लिए ΔB/Δt = 30/40 = 0.75 T/s। अत: e₁/e₂ = 1.5/0.75 = 2।

questions.text: आपको 0.016 H प्रेरकत्व की 0.81 m लम्बी और 0.02 m त्रिज्या की वायु से भरी परिनालिका की अभिकल्पना करनी है । इस परिनालिका में फेरों की संख्या होनी चाहिए
questions.text_english: You are required to design an air-filled solenoid of inductance 0.016 H having a length 0.81 m and radius 0.02 m. The number of turns in the solenoid should be
questions.solution: The inductance of a solenoid is L = μ₀n²πr²l, where n = N/l is the number of turns per unit length. So N = √(L × l / (μ₀ × πr²)). Substituting: L = 0.016 H, l = 0.81 m, r = 0.02 m, μ₀ = 4π×10⁻⁷. N² = (0.016 × 0.81) / (4π×10⁻⁷ × π × 0.0004) = 0.01296 / (4π²×4×10⁻ⁱ¹¹) ≈ 0.01296 / (15.79×10⁻ⁱ¹¹) ≈ 6.72×10⁶. N ≈ 2592. This matches option A.
questions.solution_hindi: L = μ₀N²πr²/l से N = √(Ll/(μ₀πr²)) ≈ 2592। अत: विकल्प A सही है।

questions.text: किसी परिपथ पर वोल्टता v = v₀ sin ωt अनुप्रयुक्त करने पर उस परिपथ में धारा i = i₀ sin (ωt + φ) प्रवाहित होती है । एक चक्र में इस परिपथ में औसत शक्ति खपत है –
questions.text_english: A voltage v = v₀ sin ωt applied to a circuit drives a current i = i₀ sin (ωt + φ) in the circuit. The average power consumed in the circuit over a cycle is

options_english.A: Zero
options_english.B: i₀v₀ cosφ
options_english.C: i₀v₀/2
options_english.D: (i₀v₀/2) cosφ

questions.solution: The average power consumed over one cycle is P = V_rms × I_rms × cosφ, where V_rms = v₀/√2 and I_rms = i₀/√2. Thus P = (v₀/√2)(i₀/√2) cosφ = (i₀v₀/2) cosφ. Option A is wrong because power is zero only when φ = 90°. Option B misses the factor of 1/2. Option C ignores the power factor cosφ. Option D is the standard formula for average power in AC circuits.
questions.solution_hindi: P = V_rms × I_rms × cosφ = (v₀/√2)(i₀/√2)cosφ = (i₀v₀/2)cosφ। अत: विकल्प D सही है।

questions.text: विद्युत-चुम्बकीय स्पेक्ट्रम में सूक्ष्म तरंगों से X-किरणों तक (सभी निर्वात में) होने वाले अभिलाक्षणिक परिवर्तन का निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा सही निरूपण करता है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following correctly represents the change in wave characteristics (all in vacuum) from microwaves to X-rays in electromagnetic spectrum ?

options.A: चाल: कोई परिवर्तन नहीं, तरंगदैर्ध्य: घट जाती है, आवृत्ति: कोई परिवर्तन नहीं
options.B: चाल: कोई परिवर्तन नहीं, तरंगदैर्ध्य: घट जाती है, आवृत्ति: वृद्धि होती है
options.C: चाल: वृद्धि होती है, तरंगदैर्ध्य: बढ़ जाती है, आवृत्ति: घट जाती है
options.D: चाल: कोई परिवर्तन नहीं, तरंगदैर्ध्य: बढ़ जाती है, आवृत्ति: कोई परिवर्तन नहीं

options_english.A: Speed: Remains same, Wavelength: Decreases, Frequency: Remains same
options_english.B: Speed: Remains same, Wavelength: Decreases, Frequency: Increases
options_english.C: Speed: Increases, Wavelength: Increases, Frequency: Decreases
options_english.D: Speed: Remains same, Wavelength: Increases, Frequency: Remains same

questions.solution: All electromagnetic waves travel at the same speed c = 3×10⁸ m/s in vacuum, regardless of their frequency. X-rays have much higher frequency and shorter wavelength than microwaves. Going from microwaves to X-rays, speed remains the same, wavelength decreases, and frequency increases (since c = fλ). Option B correctly captures all three changes. Option A is wrong because frequency does change. Options C and D are entirely incorrect.
questions.solution_hindi: निर्वात में सभी विद्युत-चुम्बकीय तरंगों की चाल समान (c = 3×10⁸ m/s) रहती है। सूक्ष्म तरंगों से X-किरणों की ओर जाने पर तरंगदैर्ध्य घटती है और आवृत्ति बढ़ती है। अत: विकल्प B सही है।

questions.text: दो माध्यमों '1' और '2' में प्रकाश की चाल क्रमश: v₁ और v₂ (> v₁) है । प्रकाश की किसी किरण को माध्यमों के अन्तरापृष्ठ पर पूर्ण आन्तरिक परावर्तन के लिए आपतित होना चाहिए
questions.text_english: The speed of light in two media '1' and '2' are v₁ and v₂ (> v₁) respectively. For a ray of light to undergo total internal reflection at the interface of these two media, it must be incident from

options.A: माध्यम '1' से कोण sin⁻¹(v₁/v₂) से अधिक पर
options.B: माध्यम '1' से कोण cos⁻¹(v₁/v₂) से अधिक पर
options.C: माध्यम '2' से कोण sin⁻¹(v₁/v₂) से अधिक पर
options.D: माध्यम '2' से कोण cos⁻¹(v₁/v₂) से अधिक पर

options_english.A: medium '1' and at an angle greater than sin⁻¹(v₁/v₂)
options_english.B: medium '1' and at an angle greater than cos⁻¹(v₁/v₂)
options_english.C: medium '2' and at an angle greater than sin⁻¹(v₁/v₂)
options_english.D: medium '2' and at an angle greater than cos⁻¹(v₁/v₂)

questions.solution: Total internal reflection (TIR) occurs when light travels from a denser medium to a rarer medium at an angle greater than the critical angle. Since v₂ > v₁, medium 2 is rarer (lower refractive index) and medium 1 is denser. TIR requires the ray to go from the denser medium (1) ... wait: n₁ = c/v₁ and n₂ = c/v₂. Since v₂ > v₁, n₂ < n₁, so medium 1 is denser. The critical angle θ_c = sin⁻¹(n₂/n₁) = sin⁻¹(v₁/v₂). TIR occurs from medium 1 (denser) at angle greater than θ_c. However, looking at option C: medium 2 with sin⁻¹(v₁/v₂) - this seems to match if we reconsider: n₂ = c/v₂ is actually smaller, so going from medium 2 to medium 1 would go from rarer to denser and TIR cannot occur that way. Going from medium 1 (denser, v₁ smaller) critical angle = sin⁻¹(n₂/n₁) = sin⁻¹(v₁/v₂). So the ray must be incident from medium 1 at angle greater than sin⁻¹(v₁/v₂). This matches option A. The correct answer is A.
questions.solution_hindi: TIR के लिए प्रकाश को सघन माध्यम (माध्यम 1, क्योंकि v₁ < v₂) से क्रांतिक कोण sin⁻¹(v₁/v₂) से अधिक कोण पर आपतित होना चाहिए। अत: विकल्प A सही है।

questions.text: कोई स्रोत आवृत्ति 5.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz और उत्सर्जित क्षमता 3.31 mW का एकवर्णी प्रकाश उत्पन्न करता है । इस स्रोत द्वारा औसतन प्रति सेकण्ड उत्सर्जित होने वाले फोटॉनों की संख्या है
questions.text_english: A source produces monochromatic light of frequency 5.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz and the power emitted is 3.31 mW. The number of photons emitted per second by the source, on an average is

options_english.A: 10¹⁶
options_english.B: 10²⁴
options_english.C: 10¹⁰
options_english.D: 10²⁰

questions.solution: Number of photons per second = P/(hf). Here P = 3.31×10⁻³ W, h = 6.63×10⁻³⁴ Js, f = 5.0×10¹⁴ Hz. Energy per photon = hf = 6.63×10⁻³⁴ × 5.0×10¹⁴ = 3.315×10⁻¹⁹ J. Number of photons = 3.31×10⁻³ / 3.315×10⁻¹⁹ ≈ 10¹⁶. So option A is correct. The other options represent incorrect orders of magnitude.

questions.text: नीचे दिया गया कौन सा आरेख द्रव्यमान संख्या के फलन के रूप में बंधन-ऊर्जा प्रति न्यूक्लियॉन के वक्र की सही आकृति का निरूपण करता है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following figures correctly represent the shape of curve of binding energy per nucleon as a function of mass number ?

options.A: Graph with peak around A=56, rising steeply then falling gradually
options.B: Graph with peak around A=56, rising and falling sharply
options.C: Graph with peak around A=80, with a broad hump
options.D: Graph with peak around A=80, rising and falling

options_english.A: Graph with peak around A=56, rising steeply then falling gradually
options_english.B: Graph with peak around A=56, rising and falling sharply
options_english.C: Graph with peak around A=80, with a broad hump
options_english.D: Graph with peak around A=80, rising and falling

questions.solution: The standard binding energy per nucleon curve rises sharply for light nuclei, reaches a maximum of about 8.7 MeV/nucleon near iron (A ≈ 56), and then decreases gradually for heavier nuclei. Graph A correctly shows a peak near A = 56 with a gradual declining tail for higher mass numbers. Graph B shows too sharp a peak. Graphs C and D incorrectly place the peak near A = 80. Therefore, option A is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: बंधन-ऊर्जा प्रति न्यूक्लियॉन वक्र A ≈ 56 (लोहे के पास) पर अधिकतम होता है और भारी नाभिकों के लिए धीरे-धीरे घटता है। यह आकृति केवल आरेख A में सही दिखाई गई है।

questions.text: जब कोई p-n संधि डायोड अग्रदिशिक बायसित होता है तो
questions.text_english: When a p-n junction diode is forward biased

options.A: रोधिका की ऊँचाई और हासी स्तर की चौड़ाई दोनों में वृद्धि होती है।
options.B: रोधिका की ऊँचाई में वृद्धि तथा हासी स्तर की चौड़ाई में कमी होती है।
options.C: रोधिका की ऊँचाई और हासी स्तर की चौड़ाई दोनों में कमी होती है।
options.D: रोधिका की ऊँचाई में कमी तथा हासी स्तर की चौड़ाई में वृद्धि होती है।

options_english.A: the barrier height and the depletion layer width both increase.
options_english.B: the barrier height increases and the depletion layer width decreases.
options_english.C: the barrier height and the depletion layer width both decrease.
options_english.D: the barrier height decreases and the depletion layer width increases.

questions.solution: When a p-n junction diode is forward biased, the external voltage opposes the built-in potential barrier. This reduces the barrier height (potential hill at the junction decreases). As the majority carriers are pushed towards the junction, the width of the depletion region also decreases. Therefore, both the barrier height and depletion layer width decrease. Option C is correct. Options A and B are wrong because barrier height does not increase in forward bias. Option D is wrong because depletion width decreases, not increases.
questions.solution_hindi: अग्रदिशिक बायस में बाह्य वोल्टता रोधिका (barrier) का विरोध करती है जिससे रोधिका की ऊँचाई और हासी स्तर की चौड़ाई दोनों घटती हैं। अत: विकल्प C सही है।

questions.text: मान लीजिए समान चाल से गतिमान किसी इलेक्ट्रॉन, किसी प्रोटॉन और किसी ड्यूटेरॉन से संबद्ध तरंगदैर्ध्य क्रमश: λ_e, λ_p तथा λ_d हैं । तब इन तरंगदैर्ध्यों के बीच सही संबंध है –
questions.text_english: Let λ_e, λ_p and λ_d be the wavelengths associated with an electron, a proton and a deuteron, all moving with the same speed. Then the correct relation between them is

options_english.A: λ_d > λ_p > λ_e
options_english.B: λ_e > λ_p > λ_d
options_english.C: λ_p > λ_e > λ_d
options_english.D: λ_e = λ_p = λ_d

questions.solution: The de Broglie wavelength is λ = h/(mv). For the same speed v, λ is inversely proportional to mass m. The masses are: m_e ≈ 9.1×10⁻³¹ kg (electron) < m_p ≈ 1.67×10⁻²⁷ kg (proton) < m_d ≈ 3.34×10⁻²⁷ kg (deuteron). Since m_e < m_p < m_d, we have λ_e > λ_p > λ_d. Option B is correct. Options A, C, and D do not follow from the inverse mass relationship.
questions.solution_hindi: λ = h/(mv), समान चाल पर λ ∝ 1/m। m_e < m_p < m_d, अत: λ_e > λ_p > λ_d। विकल्प B सही है।
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : हाइड्रोजन परमाणु में किसी स्थिर कक्षा में परिक्रमण करते किसी इलेक्ट्रॉन की स्थितिज ऊर्जा धनात्मक होती है ।
कारण (R) : किसी आवेशित कण की कुल ऊर्जा सदैव ही धनात्मक होती है ।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : The potential energy of an electron revolving in any stationary orbit in a hydrogen atom is positive.
Reason (R) : The total energy of a charged particle is always positive.
questions.instruction_line: नोट: इन प्रश्नों के सही उत्तरों का नीचे दिए कोड (A), (B), (C) और (D) में से चयन कीजिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Note: Select the correct answer from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सत्य हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सत्य हैं, परंतु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सत्य है, परन्तु कारण (R) असत्य है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों ही असत्य हैं।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Assertion (A) : It is difficult to move a magnet into a coil of large number of turns when the circuit of the coil is closed.
Reason (R) : The direction of induced current in a coil with its circuit closed, due to motion of a magnet, is such that it opposes the cause.

questions.solution: Assertion (A) is true: when the coil circuit is closed, moving a magnet into it induces a current that, by Lenz's law, creates a magnetic field opposing the incoming magnet. With more turns, the induced EMF is larger (E = N dΦ/dt), the opposing force is greater, and so it is harder to move the magnet. Reason (R) is also true and directly states Lenz's law — the induced current opposes the cause (motion of the magnet). R correctly and completely explains A. Hence option A is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: A सत्य है: अधिक फेरों के कारण प्रेरित emf अधिक होता है और लेन्ज़ नियम से प्रेरित धारा चुम्बक की गति का विरोध करती है। R भी सत्य है और A की सही व्याख्या करता है। विकल्प A सही है।

questions.text: यह दर्शाइए कि E⃗ = ρj⃗ ओम के नियम की ओर निर्दिष्ट करता है । उस स्थित का उल्लेख कीजिए जिसमें किसी पदार्थ के लिए ओम का नियम वैध नहीं होता है ।
questions.text_english: Show that E⃗ = ρj⃗ leads to Ohm's law. Write a condition in which the Ohm's law is not valid for a material.

key_points: E = ρj relates field and current density, deriving V = IR
Ohm's law not valid for semiconductors, vacuum tubes, electrolytes at high fields

questions.solution: We start with the relation E⃗ = ρj⃗, where E is the electric field, ρ is the resistivity and j is the current density. Consider a conductor of length l and uniform cross-sectional area A. The potential difference across it is V = El (since E is uniform). The current density is j = I/A, where I is the total current. Substituting: E = ρj gives V/l = ρ(I/A), which simplifies to V = ρ(l/A)I = RI, where R = ρl/A is the resistance. This is exactly Ohm's law, V = IR. Ohm's law is not valid for materials like semiconductors (e.g., diodes), vacuum tubes, and electrolytic solutions at very high electric fields, where the relationship between V and I is non-linear.
questions.solution_hindi: E⃗ = ρj⃗ से: V/l = ρ(I/A) ⇒ V = ρlI/A = RI जो ओम का नियम है। ओम का नियम अर्धचालकों (डायोड), निर्वात नलिकाओं और उच्च विद्युत क्षेत्र पर विद्युत अपघट्य विलयनों के लिए वैध नहीं होता।

अथवा
(b) यंग के किसी द्विझिरी प्रयोग में दो प्रकाश तरंगें, जिनमें प्रत्येक की तीव्रता I₀ है, पर्दे के उस बिन्दु पर व्यतिकरण करती हैं जिस पर पथान्तर λ/8 है । इस बिन्दु पर तीव्रता ज्ञात कीजिए ।
questions.text_english:
(a) In a diffraction experiment, the slit is illuminated by light of wavelength 600 nm. The first minimum of the pattern falls at θ = 30°. Calculate the width of the slit.
OR
(b) In a Young's double-slit experiment, two light waves, each of intensity I₀, interfere at a point, having a path difference λ/8 on the screen. Find the intensity at this point.

key_points: (a) Slit width a = λ/sinθ = 600nm/sin30° = 1200 nm = 1.2 μm
(b) Phase difference δ = 2π/λ × λ/8 = π/4; I = 4I₀cos²(π/8) = I₀(2+√2)

questions.solution:
(a) For single-slit diffraction, the condition for the first minimum is a sinθ = λ, where a is the slit width, λ = 600 nm, and θ = 30°. Therefore a = λ/sinθ = 600/sin30° = 600/0.5 = 1200 nm = 1.2 μm. The width of the slit is 1.2 μm.

(b) The phase difference corresponding to path difference λ/8 is δ = (2π/λ) × (λ/8) = π/4. The resultant intensity in Young's double-slit experiment is I = 4I₀cos²(δ/2) = 4I₀cos²(π/8). Now cos(π/8) = cos22.5° ≈ 0.924. So I = 4I₀ × (0.924)² = 4I₀ × 0.854 ≈ 3.41I₀, which equals I₀(2 + √2).

questions.text: वक्रता त्रिज्या R का गोलीय उत्तल पृष्ठ काँच (अपवर्तनांक 1.5) को वायु से पृथक करता है । वायु में इस पृष्ठ से R/2 दूरी पर स्थित किसी बिन्दु स्रोत से प्रकाश इस पृष्ठ पर पड़ रहा है । बनने वाले प्रतिबिम्ब की स्थिति और प्रकृति ज्ञात कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: A spherical convex surface of radius of curvature R separates glass (refractive index 1.5) from air. Light from a point source placed in air at distance R/2 from the surface falls on it. Find the position and nature of the image formed.

key_points: Apply refraction formula n2/v - n1/u = (n2-n1)/R
Image is virtual, on the same side as the object

questions.solution: Using the refraction formula at a spherical surface: n₂/v - n₁/u = (n₂ - n₁)/R. Here n₁ = 1 (air), n₂ = 1.5 (glass), R = +R (convex surface, centre of curvature on transmission side), u = -R/2 (object in air, sign convention). Substituting: 1.5/v - 1/(-R/2) = (1.5 - 1)/R. So 1.5/v + 2/R = 0.5/R. Therefore 1.5/v = 0.5/R - 2/R = -1.5/R. Thus v = -R. The negative sign means the image is formed on the same side as the object (in air), at a distance R from the surface. The image is virtual and erect.
questions.solution_hindi: n₂/v - n₁/u = (n₂-n₁)/R। n₁=1, n₂=1.5, u=-R/2, R=+R। 1.5/v + 2/R = 0.5/R ⇒ v = -R। प्रतिबिम्ब आभासी तथा वस्तु की ही ओर R दूरी पर है।

questions.text: बोर के हाइड्रोजन परमाणु की किसी कक्षा में किसी इलेक्ट्रॉन की ऊर्जा – 3.4 eV है । इसका कोणीय संवेग ज्ञात कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: The energy of an electron in an orbit of Bohr hydrogen atom is –3.4 eV. Find its angular momentum.

key_points: Energy = -13.6/n² eV, so n=2
Angular momentum L = nh/2π = 2.11 × 10⁻³⁴ Js

questions.solution: In the Bohr model, the energy of the nth orbit is E_n = -13.6/n² eV. Given E = -3.4 eV, we have -13.6/n² = -3.4, so n² = 4, giving n = 2. The angular momentum of an electron in the nth orbit is L = nh/(2π) = nħ. For n = 2: L = 2 × (6.63×10⁻³⁴)/(2π) = 2 × 1.055×10⁻³⁴ = 2.11×10⁻³⁴ J·s. The angular momentum of the electron is 2.11 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s.

questions.text: किसी p-प्रकार के Si-अर्धचालक को औसतन एक अपमिश्रक परमाणु प्रति 5 × 10⁷ सिलिकॉन परमाणु द्वारा अपमिश्रित (मादित) करके बनाया गया है । यदि नमूने में सिलिकॉन परमाणुओं का संख्या घनत्व 5 × 10²⁸ परमाणु प्रति घनमीटर है, तो मादन (अपमिश्रण) द्वारा नमूने में प्रति घन सेंटीमीटर निर्मित होलों (विवरों) की संख्या ज्ञात कीजिए । इस प्रकार के अपमिश्रक का एक उदाहरण भी दीजिए ।
questions.text_english: A p-type Si semiconductor is made by doping an average of one dopant atom per 5 × 10⁷ silicon atoms. If the number density of silicon atoms in the specimen is 5 × 10²⁸ atoms m⁻³, find the number of holes created per cubic centimetre in the specimen due to doping. Also give one example of such dopants.

key_points: Hole density = (5×10²⁸)/(5×10⁷) = 10²¹ m⁻³ = 10¹µ cm⁻³
Example dopant: Boron (B) or Aluminium (Al)

questions.solution: The number density of dopant atoms equals the number density of holes created. Dopant density = (Si atom density) / (ratio of Si atoms per dopant) = (5×10²⁸ m⁻³) / (5×10⁷) = 10²¹ m⁻³. Converting to per cm³: 10²¹ m⁻³ = 10²¹ / 10⁶ cm⁻³ = 10¹µ cm⁻³. Therefore, 10¹µ holes are created per cubic centimetre. An example of a p-type dopant for silicon is Boron (B) or Aluminium (Al), which are trivalent elements that create holes by accepting electrons.
questions.solution_hindi: होलों की संख्या घनत्व = (5×10²⁸)/(5×10⁷) = 10²¹ m⁻³ = 10¹µ cm⁻³। अपमिश्रक का उदाहरण: बोरॉन (B) या एल्युमीनियम (Al)।

questions.text_english:
(a) Two batteries of emfs 3V & 6V and internal resistances 0.2 Ω & 0.4 Ω are connected in parallel. This combination is connected to a 4 Ω resistor. Find : (i) the equivalent emf of the combination (ii) the equivalent internal resistance of the combination (iii) the current drawn from the combination
OR
(b) (i) A conductor of length l is connected across an ideal cell of emf E. Keeping the cell connected, the length of the conductor is increased to 2l by gradually stretching it. If R and R' are initial and final values of resistance and v_d and v_d' are initial and final values of drift velocity, find the relation between (i) R' and R and (ii) v_d' and v_d.
(ii) When electrons drift in a conductor from lower to higher potential, does it mean that all the 'free electrons' of the conductor are moving in the same direction ?

key_points: (a) Equivalent emf = 5V, equivalent internal resistance = 4/30 Ω, current ≈ 1.22 A
(b)(ii) No, free electrons have random thermal motion superimposed on the drift

questions.solution:
(a) For two batteries in parallel: equivalent emf E_eq = (E₁/r₁ + E₂/r₂)/(1/r₁ + 1/r₂) = (3/0.2 + 6/0.4)/(1/0.2 + 1/0.4) = (15 + 15)/(5 + 2.5) = 30/7.5 = 4 V. Equivalent internal resistance r_eq = r₁r₂/(r₁+r₂) = (0.2×0.4)/0.6 = 0.08/0.6 = 2/15 Ω. Current through 4Ω resistor: I = E_eq/(R + r_eq) = 4/(4 + 2/15) = 4/(62/15) = 60/62 ≈ 0.97 A.

(b)(i) When the wire is stretched from length l to 2l, its volume remains constant: A·l = A'·2l, so A' = A/2. Initial resistance R = ρl/A. Final resistance R' = ρ(2l)/(A/2) = 4ρl/A = 4R. Since EMF E is constant, V = E. Drift velocity v_d = I/nAe = E/(RnAe) ∝ 1/(RA). R' = 4R and A' = A/2, so v_d' = E/(R'nA'e) = E/(4R·n·A/2·e) = E/(2RnAe) = v_d/2. Actually v_d = eE_fieldτ/m where E_field = V/l. So v_d ∝ V/l and v_d' ∝ V/2l, giving v_d' = v_d/2. Correction: Since V=E (ideal cell), v_d = eEτ/(ml) and v_d' = eEτ/(m×2l) = v_d/2. So R' = 4R and v_d' = v_d/2.

(b)(ii) No. When electrons drift from lower to higher potential, it means there is a net drift velocity superimposed on the random thermal motion of the free electrons. The free electrons continue to move randomly in all directions due to thermal energy, but there is a small net average velocity (drift velocity) in one direction. Not all free electrons move in the same direction at any instant.

(a) E_eq = 4V, r_eq = 2/15 Ω, I ≈ 0.97 A।
(b)(i) R' = 4R; v_d' = v_d/2।

questions.text:
(a) किसी धारावाही कुण्डली के चुम्बकीय आघूर्ण की परिभाषा दीजिए तथा इसका SI मात्रक लिखिए ।
(b) क्षेत्रफल 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³ और 60 फेरों की कोई कुण्डली जिससे 2A धारा प्रवाहित हो रही है किसी ऊर्ध्वाधर तल में रखी है । किसी क्षैतिज चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र में रखे जाने पर यह 0.12 Nm बल-आघूर्ण का अनुभव करती है । इस चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र में कुण्डली को उसके व्यास के परित: 90° के कोण पर घूर्णित कराने पर उस पर कार्यरत बल-आघूर्ण 0.05 Nm हो जाता है । चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र का परिमाण ज्ञात कीजिए ।
questions.text_english:
(a) Define magnetic moment of a current-carrying coil. Write its SI unit.
(b) A coil of 60 turns and area 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³ carrying 2A current lies in a vertical plane. It experiences a torque of 0.12 Nm when placed in a uniform horizontal magnetic field. The torque acting on the coil changes to 0.05 Nm after the coil is rotated about its diameter by 90°, in the magnetic field. Find the magnitude of the magnetic field.

key_points: Magnetic moment m = NIA, SI unit A·m²
Initial torque τ₁ = mB sinθ₁ = 0.12; after 90° rotation torque τ₂ = mBsin(90+θ₁) = mBcosθ₁ = 0.05

questions.solution:
(a) The magnetic moment of a current-carrying coil is defined as the product of the number of turns, the current flowing through the coil, and the area of the coil: m = NIA. Its direction is perpendicular to the plane of the coil, given by the right-hand rule. The SI unit is A·m² (ampere-metre squared).

(b) The magnetic moment of the coil: m = NIA = 60 × 2 × 1.5×10⁻³ = 0.18 A·m². Let θ be the initial angle between m and B. Then torque τ₁ = mB sinθ = 0.12 Nm. After rotating by 90° about its diameter, the new angle is (90° + θ), so τ₂ = mB sin(90° + θ) = mB cosθ = 0.05 Nm. Squaring and adding: (mB)²(sin²θ + cos²θ) = 0.12² + 0.05². So mB = √(0.0144 + 0.0025) = √0.0169 = 0.13 Nm. Therefore B = 0.13/m = 0.13/0.18 ≈ 0.72 T. The magnitude of the magnetic field is approximately 0.72 T.

questions.text: दो लम्बी समाक्ष परिनालिकाओं S₁ और S₂ पर विचार कीजिए जिनमें प्रत्येक की लम्बाई l (>> r₂) तथा त्रिज्याएँ r₁ और r₂ (r₂ > r₁) हैं । इनमें प्रति एकांक लम्बाई फेरों की संख्या क्रमश: n₁ और n₂ है । परिनालिका S₂ के सापेक्ष परिनालिका S₁ के अन्योन्य प्रेरकत्व M₁₂ के लिए व्यंजक व्युत्पन्न कीजिए । यह दर्शाइए कि M₂₁ = M₁₂.
questions.text_english: Consider two long co-axial solenoids S₁ and S₂, each of length l (>> r₂) and of radius r₁ and r₂ (r₂ > r₁). The number of turns per unit length are n₁ and n₂ respectively. Derive an expression for mutual inductance M₁₂ of solenoid S₁ with respect to solenoid S₂. Show that M₂₁ = M₁₂.

key_points: Flux through S₁ due to current in S₂: Φ = μ₀n₂I₂ × πr₁² × n₁l
M₁₂ = μ₀πr₁²n₁n₂l
By symmetry M₂₁ = μ₀πr₁²n₁n₂l = M₁₂

questions.solution: Let a current I₂ flow through solenoid S₂ (outer, radius r₂). The magnetic field inside S₂ is B₂ = μ₀n₂I₂. This field is uniform and exists throughout the cross-section of both solenoids. The magnetic flux linked with each turn of S₁ (inner solenoid, radius r₁) is φ = B₂ × πr₁² = μ₀n₂I₂πr₁². The total number of turns in S₁ is N₁ = n₁l. Total flux linkage with S₁ is Ψ₁₂ = N₁φ = n₁l × μ₀n₂I₂πr₁². By definition, M₁₂ = Ψ₁₂/I₂ = μ₀πr₁²n₁n₂l. To show M₂₁ = M₁₂: if current I₁ flows in S₁, the field inside S₁ is B₁ = μ₀n₁I₁, but this field is confined to radius r₁. The flux through each turn of S₂ is limited to the area πr₁² (since field exists only up to r₁). Total flux linkage: Ψ₂₁ = n₂l × μ₀n₁I₁πr₁², so M₂₁ = μ₀πr₁²n₁n₂l = M₁₂. Hence M₂₁ = M₁₂.
questions.solution_hindi: S₂ में I₂ धारा से B₂ = μ₀n₂I₂। S₁ से सम्बद्ध फ्लक्स = μ₀n₂I₂πr₁² × n₁l। M₁₂ = μ₀πr₁²n₁n₂l। इसी प्रकार M₂₁ = μ₀πr₁²n₁n₂l = M₁₂।

(b) क्या उपरोक्त प्रकरण (a) में किरखोफ का पहला नियम (संधि नियम) संधारित्र की प्रत्येक पट्टिका पर वैध है ? व्याख्या कीजिए ।
questions.text_english:
(a) A parallel plate capacitor is charged by an ac source. Show that the sum of conduction current (I_c) and the displacement current (I_d) has the same value at all points of the circuit.
(b) In case (a) above, is Kirchhoff's first rule (junction rule) valid at each plate of the capacitor ? Explain.

key_points: Outside capacitor I_c flows, inside capacitor I_d = ε₀ dΦ_E/dt compensates
I_c + I_d = constant everywhere
Kirchhoff's junction rule holds if displacement current is treated equivalent to conduction current

questions.solution:
(a) Outside the capacitor, the circuit carries conduction current I_c and the displacement current I_d is zero. Inside the capacitor gap (where no physical conductor exists), conduction current I_c is zero but displacement current I_d = ε₀ dΦ_E/dt exists because the electric flux between the plates changes. Since the charge q on the capacitor equals CV, and I_c = dq/dt, while I_d = ε₀ d(E·A)/dt = ε₀A·dE/dt = ε₀A·(1/ε₀)(dσ/dt) = A·dq/(A·dt) = dq/dt = I_c. So I_d equals I_c in magnitude. Therefore, the sum I_c + I_d is the same at every point of the circuit: outside the capacitor it is I_c + 0 = I_c, and inside it is 0 + I_d = I_d = I_c.

(b) Yes, Kirchhoff's first rule (junction rule) is valid at each plate of the capacitor, provided displacement current is included. At each plate, conduction current flows in but displacement current flows out (or vice versa), so the algebraic sum of all currents (conduction + displacement) at the junction equals zero, consistent with the junction rule.
questions.solution_hindi:
(a) संधारित्र के बाहर I_c प्रवाहित होती है, अन्दर I_d = ε₀ dΦ_E/dt। सिद्ध होता है कि I_d = I_c। अत: I_c + I_d = नियत।
(b) हाँ, यदि विस्थापन धारा को भी धारा माना जाए तो किरखोफ का प्रथम नियम प्रत्येक पट्टिका पर वैध है।

questions.text_english:
(a) Draw a plot of frequency v of incident radiations as a function of stopping potential V₀ for a given photo emissive material. What information can be obtained from the value of the intercept on the stopping potential axis ?
(b) Calculate : (i) the momentum and (ii) de Broglie wavelength, of an electron with kinetic energy of 80 eV.

key_points: Plot is linear v vs V₀; x-intercept gives threshold frequency v₀ = work function/h

questions.solution:
(a) For photoelectric emission, eV₀ = hv - φ, so V₀ = (h/e)v - φ/e. The graph of v (y-axis) vs V₀ (x-axis) is a straight line. The intercept on the stopping potential axis (where v = 0) gives V₀ = -φ/e, i.e., the negative of the work function divided by e. This tells us the work function φ = e × |intercept|, which is the minimum energy required to eject an electron from the surface of the material.

(b) KE = 80 eV = 80 × 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ = 1.28×10⁻¹⁷ J.
(i) Momentum p = √(2mKE) = √(2 × 9.1×10⁻³¹ × 1.28×10⁻¹⁷) = √(2.33×10⁻⁴⁷) ≈ 4.83×10⁻²⁴ kg·m/s.
(ii) de Broglie wavelength λ = h/p = 6.63×10⁻³⁴ / 4.83×10⁻²⁴ ≈ 1.37×10⁻¹⁰ m = 1.37 Å.

(b) KE = 1.28×10⁻¹⁷ J; p ≈ 4.83×10⁻²⁴ kg·m/s; λ ≈ 1.37×10⁻¹⁰ m।

questions.solution:

(m_p = 1.007277 u; m_n = 1.008665 u, 1u = 931.5 MeV/c²)
questions.text_english:
(a) Define 'Mass defect' and 'Binding energy' of a nucleus. Describe 'Fission process' on the basis of binding energy per nucleon.
(b) A deuteron contains a proton and a neutron and has a mass of 2.013553 u. Calculate the mass defect for it in u and its energy equivalence in MeV. (m_p = 1.007277 u; m_n = 1.008665 u, 1u = 931.5 MeV/c²)

key_points: Mass defect Δm = (m_p + m_n) - m_d = 0.002389 u
Binding energy = 0.002389 × 931.5 = 2.225 MeV
Fission: heavy nucleus (low BE/A) splits into medium nuclei (high BE/A), releasing energy

questions.solution:
(a) Mass defect (Δm) is defined as the difference between the sum of masses of the constituent nucleons (protons and neutrons) and the actual mass of the nucleus: Δm = [Zm_p + (A-Z)m_n] - M. Binding energy is the energy equivalent of the mass defect: E_b = Δm × c². In fission, a heavy nucleus like ²³⁵U (which has relatively low binding energy per nucleon, ~7.5 MeV) absorbs a neutron and splits into two medium-mass nuclei (which have higher binding energy per nucleon, ~8.4 MeV). Since the products are more tightly bound, energy is released equal to the difference in total binding energies of the products and the parent nucleus.

(b) Mass defect: Δm = m_p + m_n - m_d = 1.007277 + 1.008665 - 2.013553 = 2.015942 - 2.013553 = 0.002389 u. Energy equivalence = 0.002389 × 931.5 = 2.225 MeV. The binding energy of deuteron is 2.225 MeV.
questions.solution_hindi:
(a) द्रव्यमान क्षति Δm = [Zm_p + (A-Z)m_n] - M। बंधन ऊर्जा = Δm·c²। विखंडन में भारी नाभिक कम BE/A वाला होता है; टुकड़े अधिक BE/A वाले होते हैं, अतः ऊर्जा मुक्त होती है।
(b) Δm = 0.002389 u; ऊर्जा = 2.225 MeV।

Applying the formula for image formation by a single spherical surface successively at the two surfaces of a lens, one can obtain the 'lens maker formula' and then the 'lens formula'. options_english.B: Arrow pointing up with dot on left below
options_english.C: Arrow pointing down with dot on right above

sub_questions.solution: A real image formed by a convex lens is inverted (both vertically and horizontally). The vertical arrow pointing up will appear pointing down, and the horizontal ball at the right end will appear on the left. sub_questions.text_english: Which of the following statements is incorrect ?

options_english.A: For a convex mirror magnification is always negative.
options_english.B: For all virtual images formed by a mirror magnification is positive.
options_english.C: For a concave lens magnification is always positive.
options_english.D: For real and inverted images, magnification is always negative.

sub_questions.solution: For a convex mirror, all images formed are virtual, erect and diminished. Since the image is erect (same side as object in mirror convention), magnification m = -v/u is positive (v is positive for virtual image in mirror, u is negative). So the statement 'For a convex mirror magnification is always negative' is incorrect. Options B, C, and D are correct statements.

sub_questions.text: फोकस दूरी f के किसी उत्तल लेंस को उसके मुख्य अक्ष के लम्बवत दो समान भागों में काटा गया है । इसके प्रत्येक भाग की फोकस दूरी होगी :
sub_questions.text_english: A convex lens of focal length 'f' is cut into two equal parts perpendicular to the principal axis. The focal length of each part will be :

options_english.A: f
options_english.B: 2f

sub_questions.solution: When a convex lens is cut perpendicular to the principal axis (horizontally), each half still has the same radii of curvature and the same refractive index. By the lens maker's formula, the focal length depends only on the radii of curvature and refractive index. However, each half-lens now has only one curved surface and one flat surface — it behaves like a plano-convex lens. For a plano-convex lens with the same curvature, the focal length doubles to 2f. Option B is correct.

sub_questions.text: किसी उभयोत्तल लेंस के प्रथम फोकस बिन्दु से बिम्ब की दूरी X₁ तथा प्रतिबिम्ब की लेंस के द्वितीय फोकस बिन्दु से दूरी X₂ है, तो लेंस की फोकस दूरी है
sub_questions.text_english: The distance of an object from first focal point of a biconvex lens is X₁ and distance of the image from second focal point is X₂. The focal length of the lens is

options_english.A: X₁ X₂
options_english.B: √(X₁ + X₂)
options_english.C: √(X₁ X₂)
options_english.D: √(X₂/X₁)

sub_questions.solution: This is Newton's lens equation: X₁X₂ = f², where X₁ is the distance of the object from the first focal point and X₂ is the distance of the image from the second focal point. Therefore, f = √(X₁X₂). Option C is correct. This is derived from the standard lens formula by substituting u = -(f + X₁) and v = (f + X₂).

questions.text:
चित्र में दर्शाए गए आरेख, जिसे RC श्रेणी परिपथ कहते हैं, के किसी परिपथ में कोई संधारित्र C, प्रतिरोध R का प्रतिरोधक तथा emf V की कोई आदर्श बैटरी संयोजित है। (S₂ को खुला रखते हुए) कुंजी S₁ को बन्द करने पर परिपथ पूर्ण हो जाता है तथा तुरन्त संधारित्र की पट्टिकाओं और बैटरी के टर्मिनलों के बीच आवेश का प्रवाह आरम्भ हो जाता है। संधारित्र पर आवेश में वृद्धि होती है परिणामस्वरूप संधारित्र के सिरों पर विभवान्तर V_c (= q/C) में समय के साथ वृद्धि होती है। जब यह विभवान्तर बैटरी के सिरों के बीच विभवान्तर के बराबर हो जाता है, तो संधारित्र पूर्णरूपेण आवेशित हो जाता है (Q = VC)। इस आवेशन प्रक्रिया की अवधि में संधारित्र पर आवेश q में समय के साथ परिवर्तन होता है जिसे इस प्रकार निरूपित किया जाता है – q = Q[1 – e⁻ᵗ/ᴼᶜ]
इस व्यंजक का अवकलन d/dx (eᵐˣ) = meᵐˣ का उपयोग करके आवेशन धारा प्राप्त की जा सकती है।
उस प्रकरण पर विचार कीजिए जिसमें R = 20 kΩ, C = 500 μF तथा V = 10 V
questions.text_english: A circuit consisting of a capacitor C, a resistor of resistance R and an ideal battery of emf V, as shown in figure is known as RC series circuit. As soon as the circuit is completed by closing key S₁ (keeping S₂ open) charges begin to flow between the capacitor plates and the battery terminals. The charge on the capacitor increases and consequently the potential difference V_c (= q/C) across the capacitor also increases with time. When this potential difference equals the potential difference across the battery, the capacitor is fully charged (Q = VC). During this process of charging, the charge q on the capacitor changes with time t as q = Q[1 – e⁻ᵗ/ᴼᶜ]. The charging current can be obtained by differentiating it and using d/dx (eᵐˣ) = meᵐˣ. Consider the case when R = 20 kΩ, C = 500 μF and V = 10 V.

sub_questions.text: जब कुंजी S₁ बन्द तथा S₂ खुली है तब संधारित्र पर अंतिम आवेश है –
sub_questions.text_english: The final charge on the capacitor, when key S₁ is closed and S₂ is open, is

options_english.A: 5 μC
options_english.B: 5 mC
options_english.C: 25 mC

sub_questions.solution: Final charge Q = CV = 500×10⁻⁶ F × 10 V = 5×10⁻³ C = 5 mC. Option B is correct.

sub_questions.text: पर्याप्त समय के लिए कुंजी S₁ बन्द तथा S₂ खुली रहती है। अब S₂ को बन्द तथा S₁ को खोल दिया गया है। संधारित्र पर अंतिम आवेश क्या है ?
sub_questions.text_english: For sufficient time the key S₁ is closed and S₂ is open. Now key S₂ is closed and S₁ is open. What is the final charge on the capacitor ?

options_english.A: Zero
options_english.B: 5 mC
options_english.C: 2.5 mC
options_english.D: 5 μC

sub_questions.solution: When S₂ is closed and S₁ is opened, the battery is disconnected and the capacitor discharges through the resistor R. After sufficient time, the capacitor fully discharges and the final charge on the capacitor is zero. Option A is correct.

sub_questions.text: RC के लिए विमीय सूत्र है –
sub_questions.text_english: The dimensional formula for RC is

options_english.A: [M L² T⁻³ A⁻²]
options_english.B: [M⁰ L⁰ T⁻¹ A⁰]
options_english.C: [M⁻¹ L⁻² T⁴ A²]
options_english.D: [M⁰ L⁰ T A⁰]

sub_questions.solution: RC is the time constant τ of an RC circuit, which has the dimension of time. Therefore [RC] = [T] = [M⁰ L⁰ T¹ A⁰]. Option D is correct.

sub_questions.text: कुंजी S₁ बन्द तथा S₂ खुली है। 5 सेकण्ड के पश्चात प्रतिरोधक से प्रवाहित धारा है
sub_questions.text_english: The key S₁ is closed and S₂ is open. The value of current in the resistor after 5 seconds, is

options_english.B: √e mA
options_english.C: 1/√e mA

sub_questions.solution: The charging current is i(t) = (V/R)e⁻ᵗ/ᴼᶜ. Here V/R = 10/(20×10³) = 0.5×10⁻³ A = 0.5 mA. Time constant RC = 20×10³ × 500×10⁻⁶ = 10 s. At t = 5 s: i = 0.5 × e⁻⁵/¹⁰ = 0.5 × e⁻⁰·⁵ = 0.5/e⁰·⁵ = 0.5/√e mA = 1/(2√e) mA. Wait, e⁻⁰·⁵ = 1/√e. So i = 0.5/√e mA = 1/(2√e) mA. Option A is correct. But option C is 1/√e mA. Rechecking: V/R = 10/20000 = 5×10⁻⁴ A = 0.5 mA. i(5) = 0.5 e⁻⁰·⁵ = 0.5/√e mA = 1/(2√e) mA. So correct answer is A.

questions.text_english:
(a) (i) (1) What are coherent sources ? Why are they necessary for observing a sustained interference pattern ?
(2) Lights from two independent sources are not coherent. Explain.
(ii) Two slits 0.1 mm apart are arranged 1.20 m from a screen. Light of wavelength 600 nm from a distant source is incident on the slits.
(1) How far apart will adjacent bright interference fringes be on the screen ?
(2) Find the angular width (in degree) of the first bright fringe.
OR
(b) (i) Define a wavefront. An incident plane wave falls on a convex lens and gets refracted through it. Draw a diagram to show the incident and refracted wavefront.
(ii) A beam of light coming from a distant source is refracted by a spherical glass ball (refractive index 1.5) of radius 15 cm. Draw the ray diagram and obtain the position of the final image formed.

key_points: Coherent sources: same frequency and constant phase difference
Fringe width β = λD/d = 600×10⁻⁹×1.2/10⁻⁴ = 7.2 mm
Angular width = β/D in rad = 0.0072/1.2 = 6×10⁻³ rad ≈ 0.344°

questions.solution:
(a)(i)(1) Coherent sources are those that emit light waves of the same frequency and maintain a constant phase difference between them. They are necessary for a sustained interference pattern because if the phase difference keeps changing randomly (as with independent sources), the positions of bright and dark fringes shift rapidly and the pattern averages out, becoming invisible to the eye.

(2) Two independent sources (like two separate bulbs or lamps) emit light from different atoms independently. Each atom emits a photon in a random phase, and the phase difference between the two sources changes randomly and rapidly (around 10⁸ times per second). Because the phase difference is not constant, the interference pattern keeps shifting, and no sustained pattern is observed.

(a)(ii)(1) Fringe width β = λD/d = (600×10⁻⁹ × 1.20) / (0.1×10⁻³) = 7.2×10⁻³ m = 7.2 mm. Adjacent bright fringes are 7.2 mm apart.

(2) Angular fringe width = β/D = 7.2×10⁻³/1.20 = 6×10⁻³ rad. Converting to degrees: 6×10⁻³ × (180/π) ≈ 0.344°.

(b)(i) A wavefront is defined as the locus of all points in a medium that are at the same phase of vibration at a given instant. When a plane wave (plane wavefront) falls on a convex lens, it is refracted and converges to the focal point. The refracted wavefront is a spherical surface (converging) centred on the focal point of the lens. Incident wavefront: plane (flat); refracted wavefront: spherical, converging towards the principal focus.

(b)(ii) For refraction at the first surface of the glass ball (convex, R = +15 cm, n₁ = 1, n₂ = 1.5, object at infinity u = ∞): n₂/v - n₁/u = (n₂-n₁)/R ⇒ 1.5/v = 0.5/15 ⇒ v = 45 cm from first surface (inside glass). This image acts as the object for the second surface (convex when seen from inside, now appears concave, R = -15 cm from the perspective of refraction out of glass). For second surface: n₁ = 1.5, n₂ = 1, R = -15 cm, u = 45 - 30 = 15 cm (object distance from second surface, inside glass). 1/v - 1.5/15 = (1-1.5)/(-15) = 0.5/15. So 1/v = 0.5/15 + 0.1 = 0.1333, giving v = 7.5 cm beyond the second surface. The final image is formed 7.5 cm behind the glass ball.

(a) (i) 5 μC और –1 μC के दो बिन्दु आवेश क्रमश: (–3 cm, 0, 0) और (3 cm, 0, 0) बिन्दुओं पर स्थित हैं । इस प्रदेश में किसी बाह्य विद्युत क्षेत्र E⃗ = (A/r²) r̂ को अनुप्रयुक्त किया गया है, यहाँ A = 3 × 10⁵ Vm है । इस विद्युत क्षेत्र के कारण निकाय की स्थिर विद्युत ऊर्जा में परिवर्तन परिकलित कीजिए ।

अथवा
questions.text_english:
(a) (i) Two point charges 5 μC and –1 μC are placed at points (–3 cm, 0, 0) and (3 cm, 0, 0) respectively. An external electric field E⃗ = (A/r²) r̂ where A = 3 × 10⁵ Vm is switched on in the region. Calculate the change in electrostatic energy of the system due to the electric field.
(ii) A system of two conductors is placed in air and they have net charge of +80μC and –80μC which causes a potential difference of 16 V between them.
(1) Find the capacitance of the system.
(2) If the air between the capacitor is replaced by a dielectric medium of dielectric constant 3, what will be the potential difference between the two conductors ?
(3) If the charges on two conductors are changed to +160 μC and –160 μC, will the capacitance of the system change ? Give reason for your answer.
OR

key_points: (a)(i) ΔU = q₁V(r₁) + q₂V(r₂) where V(r) = A/r; r₁=0.03m, r₂=0.03m
(ii)(1) C = Q/V = 80×10⁻⁶/16 = 5μF; (2) V' = V/K = 16/3 V; (3) No change, capacitance depends on geometry

questions.solution:
(a)(i) The external field E⃗ = (A/r²)r̂ corresponds to potential V(r) = A/r (since E = -dV/dr). Change in energy of charge q in this field = qV(r). Charge q₁ = 5μC at r₁ = 3 cm = 0.03 m: ΔU₁ = q₁ × A/r₁ = 5×10⁻⁶ × 3×10⁵/0.03 = 5×10⁻⁶ × 10⁶ = 5 J. Charge q₂ = -1μC at r₂ = 3 cm = 0.03 m: ΔU₂ = -1×10⁻⁶ × 10⁶ = -1 J. Total change in energy = ΔU₁ + ΔU₂ = 5 - 1 = 4 J.

(ii)(1) Capacitance C = Q/V = (80×10⁻⁶)/16 = 5×10⁻⁶ F = 5 μF.

(2) When air is replaced by a dielectric of constant K = 3, the capacitance increases to C' = KC = 15 μF. Since the charge remains the same (Q = 80 μC), the new potential difference V' = Q/C' = 80×10⁻⁶/15×10⁻⁶ = 16/3 ≈ 5.33 V.

(3) No, the capacitance will not change. Capacitance depends only on the geometry of the conductors (their shape, size, and separation) and the medium between them, not on the charge stored. Increasing the charge to 160 μC and -160 μC does not alter the geometry, so C remains 5 μF.
questions.solution_hindi:
(a)(i) ΔU = 5J + (-1J) = 4J।
(ii)(1) C = 5 μF; (2) V' = 16/3 V ≈ 5.33 V; (3) धारिता नहीं बदलेगी क्योंकि यह ज्यामिति पर निर्भर करती है।

questions.text:
(a) (i) किसी असमान चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र में वेग V⃗ से गतिमान कोई प्रोटॉन आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार पथ संरेखित करता है। प्रोटॉन द्वारा चला गया पथ सदैव कागज के तल में ही होता है। बिन्दु P, Q और R के निकट के प्रदेश में चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र की दिशा क्या है ? इन बिन्दुओं पर चुम्बकीय क्षेत्रों के आपेक्षिक परिमाणों के विषय में आप क्या कह सकते हैं ?

(b) (i) किसी एकसमान चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र में निलंबित किसी आयताकार धारा पाश पर कार्यरत बल आघूर्ण के लिए व्यंजक व्युत्पन्न कीजिए ।
(ii) किसी एकसमान चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र B⃗ में कोई आवेशित कण वेग V⃗ से वर्तुल मार्ग पर गमन कर रहा है। इस आवेशित कण को किसी लैड की चादर से गुजारा जाता है जिसके फलस्वरूप इसकी गति की दिशा में बिना कोई परिवर्तन हुए इसकी गतिज ऊर्जा घटकर आधी रह जाती है। इस कण के (1) पथ की त्रिज्या तथा (2) परिक्रमण के आवर्तकाल में क्या परिवर्तन होगा ?
questions.text_english:
(a) (i) A proton moving with velocity V⃗ in a non-uniform magnetic field traces a path as shown in the figure. The path followed by the proton is always in the plane of the paper. What is the direction of the magnetic field in the region near points P, Q and R ? What can you say about relative magnitude of magnetic fields at these points ?
(ii) A current carrying circular loop of area A produces a magnetic field B at its centre. Show that the magnetic moment of the loop is (2BA/μ₀)√(A/π).
OR
(b) (i) Derive an expression for the torque acting on a rectangular current loop suspended in a uniform magnetic field.
(ii) A charged particle is moving in a circular path with velocity V⃗ in a uniform magnetic field B⃗. It is made to pass through a sheet of lead and as a consequence, it looses one half of its kinetic energy without change in its direction. How will (1) the radius of its path (2) its time period of revolution change ?

key_points: (a)(i) Field perpendicular to paper; at P into page, at Q into page, at R into page; B_P > B_Q (smaller radius at P) and B_R smallest (larger radius)
(a)(ii) B = μ₀I/2r, A = πr²; m = IA = Iπr² = (2BA/μ₀)√(A/π)
(b)(ii) radius becomes 1/√2 times; time period unchanged

questions.solution:
(a)(i) The proton moves in the plane of the paper in a curved path. The magnetic force on the proton must be centripetal (towards the centre of curvature). For a positive charge moving in the plane of the paper, for the force to curve the path as shown, the magnetic field must be directed into the plane of the paper at points P, Q, and R. The radius of curvature r = mv/(qB), so a smaller radius of curvature means a stronger magnetic field. From the figure, the radius at P appears smallest, so B_P is largest; the radius at Q is intermediate; and the radius at R is largest, so B_R is smallest. Thus B_P > B_Q > B_R.

(a)(ii) For a circular loop of area A = πr², the magnetic field at the centre is B = μ₀I/(2r). From A = πr², we get r = √(A/π). So I = 2Br/μ₀ = (2B/μ₀)√(A/π). The magnetic moment m = IA = (2B/μ₀)√(A/π) × A = (2BA/μ₀)√(A/π). Hence proved.

(b)(i) Consider a rectangular loop of sides a and b carrying current I in a uniform magnetic field B. The sides of length a (parallel to B) experience no force. The two sides of length b (perpendicular to B) each experience a force F = BIb. These forces form a couple separated by the distance a sinθ, where θ is the angle between the plane of the loop and B. The torque τ = BIb × a sinθ = BIA sinθ, where A = ab is the area. In vector form, τ⃗ = m⃗ × B⃗, where m = NIA.

(b)(ii) The radius of a circular orbit is r = mv/(qB). Since KE = mv²/2, we have mv = √(2mKE). If KE becomes KE/2, the new momentum p' = √(2m·KE/2) = p/√2. So new radius r' = p'/(qB) = r/√2. The radius decreases to r/√2. The time period T = 2πm/(qB) is independent of velocity and KE, so the time period remains unchanged.
questions.solution_hindi:
(a)(i) P, Q, R पर चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र कागज के तल में अंदर की ओर है। B_P > B_Q > B_R।
(a)(ii) I = (2B/μ₀)√(A/π); m = IA = (2BA/μ₀)√(A/π) सिद्ध।
(b)(i) τ = NBIA sinθ।
(b)(ii) त्रिज्या r/√2 हो जाएगी; आवर्तकाल अपरिवर्तित रहेगा।
